summary.value: The Pictave is France's only true bantam, a naturally tiny chicken with no large version. It takes its name from the Pictavi, the ancient tribe behind the name Poitou. Around 1900 Raymond Lecointre began shaping it south of Poitiers from the small partridge-colored bantams common across Europe, and he used the hens to hatch and rear his pheasants. A standard followed in 1928. The breed nearly died out after World War Two, and rescue crosses pulled it away from the old type until breeders set out in 1998 to restore it. Birds are partridge colored with long tails, low wings and pinkish-white legs. Roosters weigh about 1.8 pounds and hens about 1.3 pounds. Hens lay around 130 small creamy white eggs a year and are superb sitters and mothers. It remains endangered.
